evidence: Core behavior has strong authored coverage: functional prompt S01 (lines 119-121) requires a real authored DOM/log edit; S02 (128-141) runs JS, complete HTML and CSS. Constraints judge lines 25-29 requires a newly saved exact record retrieved and reloaded from an independent clean browser context, accepting server-rendered data and discovered routes. S21 (426-429) proves exact Alpha/Beta save/load after reload. S22 (438-444), owned by cw_process_restart_durability (judge line 364), records every actual saved identity/title/filename/source/revision, invokes restart_app once, and compares the whole collection before a separately scored write. This fairly accepts a conforming server-rendered library with non-JSON responses, arbitrary route/field names and alternative UI layout; no false-fail was found for that alternative. However, the required complete process restart is not reliably established. Current tests/test.sh:154-159 sends TERM and waits five seconds without requiring the old process to exit; lines 160-183 start a replacement and accept any answering listener. restart_mcp.py:45-47 turns helper exit 0 into the assertion that the server was relaunched. The exact current and frozen-template test.sh SHA256 is bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa, matching the indexed original control binding; the historical generate-helper.sh restart block is byte-identical to the current block. In the original term_ignored control, helper exit was 0, old_alive was true, old PID 34 still answered after the supposed restart with memory=volatile-marker, while new PID 100 logged EADDRINUSE and ready=1 (app-restart.log:5,21). Thus the S22 success message plus fresh server readback can preserve volatile memory without proving database durability. The original normal control did replace PID 8 with 24 and retained durable-marker, demonstrating the ordinary success case. Current scripted golden evidence also reports one MCP restart, PID 16 to 347, six exact records reread, Primary revision 2 surviving and advancing to 3 after a new save; its prompt, judge and all app-file hashes match frozen bytes. These positive controls do not refute the surviving-old-process counterexample. All 102 indexed current_golden and 181 unchanged_shared_harness_controls artifact hashes were verified with zero mismatches. Relevant SHA256: golden RESULTS.json=50b312418cb362cab6d085c78f777b1be8b25ab4948ded40b672b744de620d7b; pre-results.json=d31087928b53e599e27dd38abed7b5f8f8126354820a6458b91006f9eac97070; post-results.json=8c162523c64c85299fa2597371781c5cd62e123d27ea829b57d6a365fd021099; shared control results.json=602a0a7c49b5e8d91f00d3162624563ac46de941029d47754c73aaac58cec637; original-term_ignored/app-restart.log=2bc2a2103b84affe79d5916d7b195dca778e0d561bc60927f3aa336e738666ce. The defect is in unchanged shared lifecycle machinery, not a missing task criterion. These are existing scripted/raw controls, not a full configured judge or measured model/Oracle score; no runtime probes were rerun.
counterexample: A playground that executes snippets correctly and shares saved records/revisions only in server memory can pass independent-context reads and browser reload. If its one server installs a SIGTERM handler that keeps serving (as the indexed synthetic fixture does), the canonical restart helper reports success while that same process continues serving every saved field and accepting writes. S22 then observes its expected collection and post-restart write although a genuine complete process restart would lose all saved records. The unchanged-helper failure mechanism is measured; a full defective-playground judge score is not claimed.
suggested_fix: Escalate the confirmed lifecycle defect for an authorized shared-harness correction that verifies the old process has ended and the replacement is the live listener before reporting restart success, then freeze a new candidate and remeasure durability; preserve protected shared files in this review and do not waive the restart requirement.
